overview: 1944 exchange: INS official Deyrough tells State's Smith that Kyutaro Furuguri's November 11, 1883 birth date equals Meiji 16, month 11, day 11, enclosing a Whitaker's Almanack explanation of Japan's Meiji/Taisho/Showa calendar eras and weekday names.

people.name: Kyutaro Furuguri
people.role: Subject whose birth date was being converted to the Japanese imperial calendar

people.name: S. A. Diana
people.role: Chief, Alien Parole Section, Immigration and Naturalization Service

subfiles.title: Letter from Anne R. Deyrough concerning Kyutaro Furuguri’s birth date
subfiles.from: Anne R. Deyrough, Secretary to S. A. Diana, Chief, Alien Parole Section
subfiles.to: Miss E. B. Smith, Department of State
subfiles.about: The letter supplies an almanac excerpt and converts Kyutaro Furuguri’s Gregorian birth date into the Japanese Meiji-era system.
subfiles.summary: Deyrough tells Smith that INS records give Furuguri's birth date as November 11, 1883, interpreted as Meiji 16, month 11, day 11, enclosing a calendar explanation.

subfiles.title: Whitaker’s Almanack excerpt explaining the Japanese calendar
subfiles.to: Enclosed for E. B. Smith, Department of State
subfiles.about: The excerpt describes Japan’s adaptation of the Gregorian calendar and its system of numbering years by imperial epochs.
subfiles.summary: Whitaker's Almanack excerpt explains Japan's Gregorian dates but era-based year numbering, listing Meiji/Taisho/Showa eras, 1935-36 conversion examples, month naming, and weekday names.

interest: Shows how U.S. officials converted a Japanese immigrant's birth date between Gregorian and imperial-era calendars.
